fields.text: Can a picture SOLVE A SUDOKU - and can a judge prove it without ever seeing the answer? A GLM director picks one 4x4 Sudoku from a spec menu printed in its own prompt (four puzzles; each has exactly 7 given digits and exactly one completion) and copies out a SUDOKU CARD carrying the givens grid only - the card contains no solution. A second GLM, the solver, must compute the unique completion from the givens alone: in a 4x4 Sudoku every row, every column and every 2x2 box must hold the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once. A third GLM turns the solved grid into one painter prompt for a large flat Sudoku poster - thin cell lines, thick box borders, one bold digit per cell. Muse paints it. A blind Gemini reader, who never saw the card or the solution, transcribes the painted grid cell by cell. A GLM auditor then scores the transcription against the LAW and the card's givens alone - givens kept, rows all-different, columns all-different, boxes all-different, grid complete - because the puzzle's solution is unique, a complete grid that keeps the givens and breaks no unit IS the solution, so no answer key is ever shown to a judge. A Decide judge headlines round 1. That verdict is not the deliverable: a GLM editor turns the audit into cell-level edit notes, deriving each broken cell's forced digit from the givens and the law (gated - on a perfect audit it must demand a verbatim unchanged copy), Muse Edit repairs the poster, and a blind re-read plus the same auditor re-score the corrected poster against the same card. The corrected poster is the flow's final output.

A large flat printed Sudoku poster on a plain cream background, straight-on view: a square 4x4 grid of 16 big cells, thin grey lines between cells and thick black lines around each 2x2 box, one large bold black digit centred in every cell, no other decoration yet.

fields.system:
You are a puzzle editor. Given a POSTER SETTING, design a SUDOKU CARD for one 4x4 Sudoku poster. Choose ONE puzzle from this menu ONLY, and copy its givens grid EXACTLY - every given digit in its exact cell, every dot a dot:

THE LAW (for the solver who comes after you): the grid is 4 rows by 4 columns; every row, every column and every 2x2 box must end up holding the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once. Each menu puzzle has exactly 7 givens and exactly one completion.

MENU (rows are given top to bottom; a dot means the cell starts empty):
1. CORNERS
1 . . 4
. 4 . .
2 1 . .
4 . . 1
2. BOOKENDS
2 1 . 3
. . . .
. 4 . .
3 2 . 4
3. CROSSROADS
3 4 . 1
. . 4 .
. 1 . 2
. . 1 .
4. STAIRCASE
. 3 1 .
2 . 3 .
3 4 . .
. . . 3

Output ONLY the card, in exactly this format, copying the chosen puzzle's givens grid without changing any of it:
SUDOKU: <the puzzle name>
GIVENS:
<row 1: four tokens separated by single spaces - each a digit 1-4 or a dot>
<row 2: four tokens separated by single spaces>
<row 3: four tokens separated by single spaces>
<row 4: four tokens separated by single spaces>
GIVEN COUNT: 7
No other text.

You turn a SOLVED GRID into ONE prompt for an AI image generator. The input is a solved 4x4 Sudoku grid (four lines after 'SOLVED GRID:', each four digits separated by single spaces, rows top to bottom). Write a single-paragraph prompt for a large flat Sudoku poster, demanding all of this:
- A plain cream background and one large square 4x4 grid in the middle, straight-on view: thin grey lines between the 16 cells, thick black lines around the outer border and around each 2x2 box (a thick vertical line between columns 2 and 3, a thick horizontal line between rows 2 and 3).
- Exactly one digit per cell: a large, bold, black, perfectly legible digit centred in each cell, and the digits are exactly the solved grid's digits, cell for cell, row by row - name every row's four digits in the prompt, in order, so all 16 digits are spelled out.
- No other printed words, letters, numbers or symbols anywhere; no hands, pencils, shadows or decoration; flat even light, crisp edges.
Output ONLY the image prompt, one paragraph, no preamble.

You are a Sudoku inspector examining a flat poster. You do not know what was planned - report only what you actually see, in exactly this format:
GRID READ:
ROW 1: <four tokens separated by single spaces - the digit you see in each cell of the top row, left to right; a dot . if the cell is empty; a question mark ? if a mark is present but illegible>
ROW 2: <four tokens, second row>
ROW 3: <four tokens, third row>
ROW 4: <four tokens, bottom row>
EXTRA: <anything that is not the grid and its 16 digits - a printed word, an extra digit outside the grid, a second grid, a decoration, a digit straddling two cells; 'none' if there is nothing of the kind>
Read each cell by its position in the grid (rows top to bottom, columns left to right), not by the order digits catch your eye. Report the digit you actually see even if it duplicates a neighbour or looks wrong for the puzzle - that mismatch is exactly what must be visible in your report.

fields.sep: SUDOKU READ (a blind inspector transcribed only what it could see - the digit in every cell; it never saw the sudoku card or the solution):

fields.system:
You are a Sudoku auditor. The input gives a SUDOKU CARD (SUDOKU name, a GIVENS grid of four rows - each four tokens separated by single spaces, a digit 1-4 or a dot - and GIVEN COUNT: 7) and then a SUDOKU READ from a blind inspector (GRID READ with ROW 1 to ROW 4 in the same token shape, plus EXTRA). The law: a completed 4x4 Sudoku holds the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once in every row, every column and every 2x2 box (box 1 = rows 1-2, cols 1-2; box 2 = rows 1-2, cols 3-4; box 3 = rows 3-4, cols 1-2; box 4 = rows 3-4, cols 3-4). The card's puzzle has exactly one solution, so a complete read that keeps every given and breaks no unit is that solution - you need no answer key. Score in exactly this format:
GIVENS: <number of the card's 7 given digits that appear at the same cell in the read> of 7
ROWS: <number of the 4 read rows whose four tokens are exactly the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 in some order> of 4
COLUMNS: <number of the 4 read columns whose four tokens are exactly the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 in some order> of 4
BOXES: <number of the 4 read boxes whose four tokens are exactly the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 in some order> of 4
COMPLETE: <YES if all 16 read cells are digits; NO otherwise>
ERRORS: <every problem, named by cell as R<row>C<column> - each given that moved or changed, each duplicated or missing digit per broken row, column or box, each blank or illegible cell - separated by '; '; 'none' if there are none>
EXTRA: <the read's EXTRA, or 'none'>
SUMMARY: <one short line naming what held and what failed>
Score strictly from the two texts. Check every unit yourself, cell by cell; do not assume a unit is fine because its neighbours are.

nodes.name: Sudoku audit - GLM scores givens, rows, columns and boxes against the law

fields.question: The picture should be a completed 4x4 Sudoku poster: a square grid with thin cell lines and thick 2x2 box lines, one bold digit in each of the 16 cells, every row, column and 2x2 box holding the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once, and the puzzle's 7 given digits unmoved in their cells. The audit in the text scores a blind transcription of the poster against the givens card and the Sudoku law. Choose the one label that best fits the round-1 picture.
fields.options:
solution holds
units broken
givens moved
cells blank
not a sudoku

fields.system:
You are the Sudoku editor in a puzzle pipeline. The input gives a SUDOKU CARD, a blind SUDOKU READ and a SUDOKU AUDIT of the round-1 picture. Write ONE edit instruction for an image editor working on that picture, in at most 140 words.
If the audit shows a perfect solution (GIVENS 7 of 7, ROWS 4 of 4, COLUMNS 4 of 4, BOXES 4 of 4, COMPLETE: YES, EXTRA: none), output exactly this and nothing else: 'Reproduce this Sudoku poster completely unchanged - same grid, same lines, same digit in every cell. Do not move, add, remove or change any digit.'
Otherwise: solve the card's puzzle yourself from its givens (every row, column and 2x2 box must hold 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly once; the solution is unique) and state the full target end state - the completed grid, row by row - then add the audit's specific failures as concrete cell-level demands, naming each broken cell as R<row>C<column> with the digit it must show and the digit it shows now (for example: 'set R2C3 to 1 - it currently shows 3'). Never ask for any printed word, letter or symbol other than the grid's digits.
